questions.story: An email impersonating a regular shipping vendor arrives containing an 'OVERDUE INVOICE' attached as a compressed .zip archive.
questions.question: What Secure Email Gateway (SEG) rule provides the strongest initial boundary defense against malicious attachments?
options: Configuring mail gateway policies to block or sandbox incoming .zip, .exe, or macro-enabled files from unverified external senders
Asking employees to hover over attachment filenames before downloading
Increasing email inbox storage capacity to handle large files
Forwarding all incoming attachments to personal email accounts
questions.feedback: Automated email filtering blocks high-risk file types at the network perimeter before they ever land in an employee inbox.

questions.story: A supplier email arrives requesting that future invoice payments be remitted to a new, updated bank account or mobile money number.
questions.question: Which organizational process control prevents financial loss from modified payment instructions?
options: Replying directly to the email asking if the new bank details are genuine
Out-of-band verification (confirming changes directly with the vendor via a trusted, pre-established phone number)
Processing the payment immediately to avoid late fee penalties
Posting a public inquiry on social media
questions.feedback: Never verify payment account changes using contact info provided in the suspicious message itself; always use an independent, verified channel.

questions.story: An employee double-clicks an attached document containing a hidden malicious script designed to execute in the background.
questions.question: Which security solution detects and isolates unauthorized background execution on a local endpoint device?
options: Disconnecting the monitor from the desktop computer
Active Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) or Antivirus software with real-time process execution monitoring
questions.feedback: Modern EDR tools monitor running system processes and terminate suspicious behavior (like a PDF spawning a command shell) in real time.

questions.story: During a Business Email Compromise (BEC), attackers often manipulate email routing so they can read incoming financial replies silently.
questions.question: Which detection indicator signals that an attacker is secretly monitoring financial transactions?
options: Automated alerts flagging newly created inbox rules that forward messages containing words like 'invoice' or 'payment' to external addresses
High CPU usage on the local office workstation
Receiving duplicate copies of promotional newsletters
Slower internet speed during peak office hours
questions.feedback: Covert forwarding rules are a classic BEC indicator used by threat actors to monitor payment discussions without interfering with the primary user.
